name: Unverferth Manufacturing Co., Inc.
old_description: Our Delphos facility is located in Northwest Ohio and is the founding home of the Killbros brand. Purchased by Unverferth in 1993, this facility specializes in producing key components and assemblies for multiple product lines, including seed tenders, ATV sprayers, header transports and smaller grain carts. With a strong focus on precision machining, welding, and fabrication, the Delphos location manufacturers some of the highest quality agricultural machinery in the industry.
about:
Unverferth Manufacturing Co., Inc. was founded in 1948 in Kalida, Ohio, by father-and-son duo Lawrence G. and Richard Unverferth. The pair started L.G. Unverferth Manufacturing with a loan backed by family war bonds, initially producing combine shucker control levers and soon after introducing bolt-on dual-wheel extensions for tractors. The company incorporated as Unverferth Mfg. Co., Inc. The business has remained family-owned and operated throughout its history.

The company manufactures a broad line of agricultural equipment across four production sites in Kalida and Delphos, Ohio; Shell Rock, Iowa; and a fourth location. Core processes include precision machining, welding, fabrication, powder coating, and final assembly, supported by in-house product design and engineering. The product portfolio spans grain carts and wagons, header transports, seed tenders, fertilizer applicators, tillage tools, augers and conveyors, and agricultural dual, replacement, and specialty wheel systems. These products are sold under six brands — Blu-Jet, Brent, Orthman, Parker, Top Air, and Unverferth — through eight sales and distribution branches in the United States and Canada.

Unverferth serves row-crop and livestock farmers, custom applicators, and agricultural retailers across North America. Its equipment is used in grain handling (Brent grain carts up to 1,500-bushel capacity), fertilizer application (Blu-Jet anhydrous ammonia and liquid applicators, Top Air sprayers with T-Tank design and steerable hitch), tillage (Orthman 1tRIPr strip-till, Rolling Harrow soil conditioner), and seed handling (Seed Runner bulk tenders, Parker Seed Chariot). The company also supplies replacement and dual-wheel systems for tractors and combines.

Unverferth states its mission is to help the farming community become more efficient through innovation and quality manufacturing. The company emphasizes its patent portfolio — covering dual-wheel mounting systems, grain cart unloading augers, seed tender conveyors, and sprayer section-control technology — as a differentiator, along with the ability to control design, fabrication, and coating under one roof at its Kalida headquarters.

name: Urschel Laboratories Inc
old_description: Urschel is the world’s leading manufacturer of industrial food cutting machines, helping processors across the globe achieve precise, high-volume results. Our equipment is engineered to handle nearly any product — from fruits, vegetables, and potatoes to meat, cheese, baked goods, comitrol processing, and pet food. Whether you need perfect slices, uniform dices, fine purees, or controlled granulation, Urschel delivers reliable performance and unmatched quality.
about:
Urschel Laboratories was founded in 1910 in Valparaiso, Indiana, by William E. Urschel, who invented the Gooseberry Snipper. The company, now headquartered in Chesterton, Indiana, became 100% employee-owned through an ESOP on March 3, 2016, with Patrick Urschel serving as CEO.

The company designs and builds industrial food cutting machines — dicers, slicers, shredders, and milling equipment — capable of slicing, dicing, strip cutting, shredding, granulating, milling, and pureeing a wide range of products from fruits and vegetables to meat, cheese, and pet food. Its product line includes models such as the Little Gem Aspire Dicer, M VersaPro Dicer, DiversaCut series, Sprint series, Affinity series, and Model M6. Urschel serves customers in over 130 countries and has operated across four generations.

Its equipment is used by food processors worldwide for applications such as slicing potatoes, dicing tomatoes, shredding lettuce and cheese, pureeing nut milks and vegetables, milling nut butters, and processing meat and poultry. The machines serve the broader food processing industry, including fruit, vegetable, potato, meat, cheese, baked goods, and pet food segments.

The company traces its competitive edge to its founding principle — a machine that could do the work of 100 workers in a day — and continues to invest in patented cutting technology through its Innovation & Development team. The employee-ownership model is cited as a driver of long-term commitment and product reliability.

name: Uzelac Industries Inc.
old_description: Uzelac Industries was founded in 2003 by Michael Uzelac following the acquisition of Poja Sheetmetal, and later Duske Engineering in 2006. Drawing on decades of experience in manufacturing leadership, Michael launched the company with a focus on contract fabrication, which evolved into a specialized operation designing and manufacturing direct-fired rotary dryers.
about:
Uzelac Industries was founded in 2003 by Michael Uzelac in Greendale, Wisconsin, after he acquired Poja Sheetmetal (established 1956) and later Duske Engineering (established 1980). The family-owned company began as a contract fabrication shop and evolved into a specialist in direct-fired rotary dryer design and manufacturing.

The company engineers and builds custom direct-fired rotary drying systems, delivered factory-assembled for minimal on-site installation. It also provides turnkey fabrication services for large equipment OEMs, with capabilities that include brake bending, rolling, shearing, punching, MIG and TIG welding, and waterjet cutting. The plant houses a 25-ton crane bay and a 10-ton crane bay, each with 22.5 feet of clear hook height. The workforce consists of journeymen fabricators and engineers with over 40 years of experience in dryer design, and the firm holds several U.S. patents.

Uzelac serves the hemp, poultry, biomass, rendering, biosolids, and gasification industries. In poultry, it has supplied rotary drying systems to Herbruck’s Poultry Ranch, Michael Foods, Foster Farms, and Tyson for more than 30 years. Its drying systems are installed worldwide.

The business traces its roots to the craftsmanship of Poja Sheetmetal and the engineering of Duske Engineering, carrying forward core values of integrity, customer satisfaction, and innovation. Michael Uzelac launched the venture to combine those legacies into a single design-build manufacturer of rotary drying equipment.

name: VESCO-NM
old_description: VESCO-NM manufactures state of the art proprietary Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) systems and components as well as components for Metal Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) systems. We specialize in MBE, MOCVD and semiconductor cleanroom tools decommissioning, decontamination and installations.
about:
VESCO-NM is based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The company was founded in 2009 by Dr. Abdel-Rahman EL-Emawy, who earned his Ph.D. from Colorado State University in 1996 with a dissertation on the growth of II/VI materials by MBE. After a career as an aircraft avionics engineer and a research professor at the University of New Mexico’s Center for High Technology Materials, Dr. El-Emawy established VESCO-NM to commercialize his expertise in MBE and MOCVD equipment.

The company designs and manufactures proprietary Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) systems—including the Ultima 310 model—and components such as valved crackers, effusion cells, RF plasma sources, and heaters. It also produces components for Metal Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) systems. Beyond new equipment, VESCO-NM provides decommissioning, decontamination, installation, and refurbishment services for semiconductor cleanroom tools worldwide. Its Albuquerque facility houses a machine shop with CNC milling, CNC lathe, wire EDM, water jet, and welding stations, plus a clean room for assembly and testing and CAD workstations for design and simulation.

VESCO-NM serves research facilities, universities, private industry, and government agencies across the globe, with over 300 customers served. Its equipment supports applications in semiconductor crystal growth, LED manufacturing, renewable energy, thin-film technologies, and consumer electronics. The company has worked with most existing MBE and MOCVD system platforms.

Dr. El-Emawy founded the business to deliver smart designs and the highest quality products at reasonable prices, backed by world‑class customer service and a commitment to meeting deadlines. The company emphasizes unique equipment designs that enable innovation in materials growth and deposition.

VSE provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing services, including PCBA design and engineering, printed circuit board assembly (from prototype through high-volume production), box build assembly, wire harness and cable assembly, and comprehensive testing such as in-circuit, functional, environmental, HIPOT, and X-ray inspection. The San Jose facility focuses on new product introduction (NPI) and quick-turn prototyping, while the Reno site handles larger production runs. The company serves industries including aerospace, biotechnology, telecommunications, semiconductor, medical devices, clean technology, automotive, renewable energy, and industrial equipment. Customers range from entrepreneurial teams launching first products to established firms requiring domestic manufacturing with regulatory compliance.

VSE’s stated differentiation rests on five pillars: scalable production with a boutique approach, supply chain resilience through domestic assembly and verified components, speed to market via streamlined handoffs and direct communication, secure transparent partnerships protecting intellectual property, and total quality compliance with IPC and ISO standards at every stage. name: Vermont Custom Handrails and Metalwork LLC
old_description: Vermont Custom Handrails & Metalwork was founded in 2021 by James Lambert, a master fabricator with over twenty years of specialized experience. James works directly with homeowners and architects to transform structural requirements into artistic centerpieces.
about:
Vermont Custom Handrails & Metalwork operates from a fabrication shop in Hyde Park, Vermont. The company was founded in 2021 by James Lambert, a master fabricator with more than twenty years of specialized metalworking experience. Lambert started the business to work directly with homeowners and architects, translating structural requirements into custom architectural centerpieces.

The shop produces custom stair and railing systems for both residential and commercial projects. Capabilities include floating stairs, wood-framed and steel-framed staircases, stainless steel handrail and cable railing systems, spiral staircases, and ADA-compliant railings. Every component is custom-fabricated on site using high-grade stainless steel by a team whose combined fabrication experience exceeds sixty years. The company also offers turnkey packages that cover design, fabrication, and installation, along with optional LED lighting integrated into handrails and monorail stairs.

Clients range from private homeowners building lakefront retreats and mountain lodges to architects and commercial contractors needing code-compliant railing systems. old_description: Wapsie has successfully produced products in the dairy industry since 1906.  Although the dairy industry has shown little growth over the years, Wapsie has continuously adjusted its manufacturing processes and equipment to compete in the volatile landscapes of the dairy industry.  Wapsie Valley Creamery continues to invest in new equipment that is able to process more milk more efficiently to obtain the best yields in its products.  Although the company has grown over the years, the company is still a relatively small company in the dairy industry.
about:
Wapsie Valley Creamery, a family-owned dairy processor, has operated in Independence, Iowa since 1906. The company began as a local creamery and remains under family ownership.

The company manufactures cheese, lactose, and whey products at its Independence processing plant, sourcing raw milk from over 170 independent dairy farms across eastern Iowa, southwestern Wisconsin, and northwestern Illinois. A workforce of approximately 140 employees runs the facility, which has continuously updated its manufacturing processes and equipment to handle larger milk volumes and improve product yields.

Cheese is sold to large wholesale companies that cut and shred it into private-label packages for retail distribution. Lactose goes to food manufacturers for use in confectionery, sweeteners, and dairy blends. Reduced-lactose whey is supplied to wholesalers for processed cheese, cheese spreads, and calf milk replacer.

Wapsie Valley Creamery states that its point of difference is a commitment to surpass normal quality standards. The plant operates under inspection by the USDA, FDA, and state agencies, maintains an on-site quality assurance laboratory, and uses outside labs for pathogen testing, while ongoing equipment upgrades aim to boost processing efficiency.

old_description: Founded by siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward, the company is committed to domestic manufacturing and building long-term partnerships by delivering high-quality, made-in-USA parts with unmatched flexibility.
about:
Ward's Manufacturing operates from Warren, Rhode Island, where siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward founded the company in 2022. The brother‑sister team, both former buyers of fabrication services, launched the shop after experiencing the difficulties of sourcing reliable domestic metalwork. Their family background includes a grandfather who was a carpenter rebuilding post‑war London and another who worked as an auto mechanic and metalworker, instilling a service‑oriented trade ethic. The business is certified as a woman‑owned small business.

The shop provides fiber laser cutting (3 kW, 5 × 10 ft bed, ±0.001″ cut tolerance), CNC press brake bending (190‑ton, up to 10 ft length), machining (thread cutting, countersinking, counterboring, reaming, inserts, laser etching), and in‑house finishing (#4 brushed, vibratory tumbling, glass bead blasting, orbital sanding). Product design and engineering support covers CAD creation from sketches, design optimization, and GD&T expertise. Value‑added services include powder coating, wet painting, anodizing, assembly, welding, and a range of surface treatments. There is no minimum order quantity; the company runs from single prototypes to production runs of tens of thousands of units and has shipped to 43 U.S. states and four Canadian provinces.

Customers span aerospace and defense, marine and boat building, robotics and automation, electronics and enclosure fabrication, renewable energy (wind turbine and solar components), medical devices, industrial equipment, automotive, and niche sectors such as shellfish aquaculture, art, and custom signage. The client base consists mainly of small‑to‑mid‑sized OEMs and manufacturers across North America who require tight tolerances and fast turnaround.

Ward's differentiates itself with a 99 % quality rate, domestic production in Warren, and a collaborative approach that includes expedited 24‑ to 48‑hour rush delivery, no minimum orders, and woman‑owned/green‑manufacturer certifications that help clients meet supplier‑diversity and sustainability goals.

about:
Founded in 1910 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Wayne Mills is a family-owned textile manufacturer now in its fifth generation. The company began weaving twill tapes, bindings, and light webbings at a time when steam was produced from coal and yarn arrived by horse and wagon.

Today the firm operates a 150,000-square-foot complex of nine buildings on four acres in a historic Philadelphia district. A workforce of more than 60 runs warping and weaving machines, a high-speed bleaching range, and an on-site dyehouse equipped with 16 skein dyeing machines and a computer-controlled Mageba continuous dye range. The facility also houses finishing, coating, lamination, and custom cutting and packaging lines. Stock items such as cotton tapes (styles 6210, 5541, 5526, 4214, 5533) and polyester and nylon webbings are kept on hand for rapid shipment.

Wayne Mills serves apparel, bindings, military-specification, and bag-and-strap markets. Customers include brands such as Analog Watch Company and government-related buyers; the company's military-specification webbings meet defense requirements. Its textile design service helps clients develop custom narrow fabrics from concept to production.

The company emphasizes small dye-lot minimums of just 15 pounds—far below the industry standard of 500–1,000 pounds—fast turnaround enabled by large inventory, and a tenured team averaging 25-plus years of service. Environmental recognition from the City of Philadelphia for wastewater treatment and membership in the Narrow Fabric Institute underscore its operational standards. All products are manufactured in the USA.

Beyond alignment tools, the Oregon facility manufactures drink holders, quick-disconnect tools, transmission plugs, seal installers, and timing chain tools without outsourcing.

Customers include manufacturers of aftermarket clutch kits for consumer automobiles, heavy-duty trucks, and agricultural equipment across North America, Central America, and overseas markets. West Automotive works directly with clients' R&D departments to develop custom tools for new and existing applications, guaranteeing 100 percent fill rates on every purchase order and on-time delivery to meet production schedules.

West’s differentiator is a fully integrated, no-outsource operation backed by a 100 percent product-quality guarantee that offers replacement or full refund. The founder’s original insight — precision alignment for manual transmissions — still drives a product line that emphasizes waste-free molding and rapid response to evolving engine platforms.

WMS is a leader in the region for carbon steel as well as first and second stage processed parts. WMS services Alabama, Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri and Tennessee with next day deliveries while also maintaining weekly shipments nationwide. The combination of holding a huge inventory with processing capabilities has made WMS one of the most respected and reliable service centers in the Southeast.
about:
West Memphis Steel Corporation operates from West Memphis, Arkansas, where it was founded in 1978. The company has been owned since 1988 by President and CEO Byron P. Besser, who entered the business as the nephew of co‑owner Louis Barg and worked in sales before acquiring the operation.

The firm runs a full‑line hot‑rolled steel service center with three campuses in the West Memphis area. Its processing capabilities include precision sawing, shearing, brake pressing, flat‑bed laser and plasma cutting, tube laser cutting, robotic welding, drilling/tapping, and assembly and kitting. The company stocks a wide range of carbon‑steel products — hot‑rolled and pickled‑and‑oiled sheet, plate, structural shapes, tubing, pipe, bar grating, and expanded metal — and emphasizes just‑in‑time processing with next‑day delivery across Alabama, Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri, and Tennessee, plus weekly shipments nationwide.

West Memphis Steel serves manufacturers, fabricators, and construction firms throughout the Southeast that require carbon‑steel plate, sheet, and structural components processed to first‑ and second‑stage specifications. Its customer base includes companies needing cut‑to‑length blanks, welded assemblies, and kitted kits for downstream production.

The company states its mission is to improve people’s lives and maintain a family‑style workplace where entrepreneurial spirit thrives, while delivering a customer‑service experience that exceeds expectations and enables customers to excel. It highlights its long‑tenured workforce — some with 30‑year careers — as a key differentiator.

The shop also delivers prototyping, reverse engineering, and maintenance and repair services for engines, prime movers, and turbochargers.

Customers include industrial equipment manufacturers, renewable energy project developers, automotive and aerospace suppliers, and mining and marine operators requiring durable components for extreme conditions.

WVMS emphasizes its skilled engineering team, comprehensive in-house capabilities from machining through finishing, and a customer-centric approach that prioritizes urgency and reliability to minimize downtime for critical industrial systems. The firm highlights global shipping reach and a commitment to quality assurance on every project.

name: Western Energy Systems
old_description: Western Energy Systems is a distributor and systems integrator of combined heat and power (CHP) and distributed generation solutions, including switchgear. Offers fuel gas compressors, battery storage and other power systems, serving utility, commercial and industrial clients.
about:
Western Energy Systems, operating as Northeast-Western Energy Systems USA, LLC (NES-WES), is headquartered in Brea, California. The company traces its roots to 1964 and was acquired by the INNIO Group in 2023, bringing additional resources to its power generation and microgrid businesses. With over 50 years of experience in reciprocating engine power applications, NES-WES has evolved into a full-service integrator of combined heat and power (CHP) and distributed generation (DG) solutions.

NES-WES designs, engineers, and maintains CHP and DG systems ranging from 50 kW to 22 MW, with a focus on gaseous fuels including natural gas, biogas, propane, and syngas. The firm provides end-to-end integration of balance-of-plant components such as heat recovery, fuel gas handling, emissions control, cooling systems, switchgear, transformers, and power plant controls. Its engineering team performs electrical system studies, protective relaying, and relay coordination, while field project managers oversee installation, pre-commissioning, startup, and acceptance testing. The company employs between 200 and 499 people.

The company serves utility, industrial, commercial, institutional, and governmental customers. Notable projects include the Bergen County Wastewater Treatment plant, Covidien's New Haven CHP installation, Mount Joy Wire, landfill-gas-to-energy facilities, High Sierra California Cogeneration, and Techni-Cast industrial cogeneration. Clients typically seek to reduce energy costs, improve resilience, and lower carbon footprints.

NES-WES emphasizes a balance of innovative solutions and time-tested approaches, aiming to exceed customer expectations. The 2023 acquisition by INNIO Jenbacher strengthened its position in the power generation and microgrid markets, allowing it to offer fully integrated, climate-neutral energy solutions from a single source.

name: Western Washington Sheet Metal
old_description: Angela joined the Western Washington Sheet Metal JATC in 2017 after transferring from the SM JATC in Las Vegas, where she had been employed since 2008. Her introduction to the sheet metal industry came through a friend who worked at the JATC and recommended it as a promising career path.
about:
Western Washington Sheet Metal JATC operates as a non-profit union training center headquartered in Everett, Washington, with a second campus in DuPont. The joint apprenticeship committee traces its roots to a sheet metal apprenticeship tradition spanning over 100 years, with the modern program structure in place since 1973. It is governed by a committee of six labor trustees from SMART Local 66 and six management trustees from SMACNA Western Washington.

The JATC runs a five-year sheet metal apprenticeship combining on-the-job training with classroom instruction across four disciplines: general sheet metal fabrication and installation, testing adjusting and balancing (TAB), HVAC service, and residential sheet metal. At any given time roughly 500 apprentices are enrolled, and the program graduates approximately 98 journey-level workers each year. Instruction is delivered by seven full-time instructors supported by three administrators and two support staff, collectively holding nearly 210 years of industry experience. Facilities include welding labs certified for SMAW and FCAW processes, and curriculum covers commissioning, controls, energy auditing, smoke control, and Bluebeam.

Graduates enter the workforce through 72 signatory contractors — ranging from small shops to large mechanical firms such as MacDonald-Miller, Hermanson Company, McKinstry, and PSF Mechanical — who employ apprentices and journey workers across commercial construction, healthcare facilities, data centers, and institutional projects. The DuPont campus hosts the SMART Heroes program, providing a direct entry route for active-duty military personnel and veterans. The program also partners with Bates Technical College for associate-degree credit.

The committee’s stated mission is to bring labor and management together to develop a highly skilled, competitive workforce for the evolving sheet metal industry. By offering tuition-free training, zero student debt, and a clear path to union wages and benefits — including retirement, family medical, dental, and vision — the JATC positions the apprenticeship as a career alternative to traditional college pathways.

Westfield Sheet Metal Works, Inc. operates from Kenilworth, New Jersey, where it has been in business since 1928. The company began as a union shop affiliated with Sheet Metal Workers Union Local 22 and remains a union-affiliated fabricator. No individual founders are named in the available records.

The firm provides custom metal fabrication from design through installation, handling projects that range from small machine guards to 10‑foot‑by‑10‑foot plenums requiring crane lifts. Its 50,000‑square‑foot manufacturing and office facility sits on a 100,000‑square‑foot lot and is equipped for shearing, bending, welding, polishing, painting, quality control, and delivery. Engineering and project management teams guide each job from initial sketch or CAD drawing to final shipment.

Westfield serves architectural, commercial, construction, manufacturing, and historic‑restoration markets. Completed projects include the Streicker Bridge, light pylons for Gantry Plaza, Hunters Point South Park, Madison Square Garden, and Hunts Point Landing. The shop also produces custom stainless‑steel components for concession trailers and replicates historic window parts for landmark buildings.

The company emphasizes end‑to‑end control, with an in‑house engineering and project management staff that oversees every step from design to installation. Customers cite the firm’s dedication to quality service, on‑time and on‑budget delivery, and the ability to handle both one‑off and repeat production work.

about:
Westshore Electronics was founded in 2003 in Holland, Michigan. The company began as an engineering-focused operation providing electronic and mechanical design alongside software development, aiming to help customers move from concept to production.

Today the firm operates as a single-source electronics manufacturer, offering double-sided surface-mount assembly, flexible and metal-core PCB assembly, through-hole and mixed-technology builds, automated selective wave soldering, microcontroller programming, and full functional testing. Its equipment handles fine-pitch placement down to 01005 packages and ball-grid-array components, and it provides conformal coating, cable assemblies, and finished-goods box builds. The shop supports IPC Class 2 and 3 work and runs PPAP-capable processes.

Westshore serves small and mid-tier manufacturers in the medical, industrial-controls, durable-goods, and inspection-lighting sectors. Customers typically need embedded control systems, high-density circuit boards, LED PCBAs, instrument lighting, and electromechanical controls, and the company manages component sourcing and supply-chain logistics alongside design and production.

The company emphasizes a quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015, reinforced by on-site IPC training, a proprietary Track-Trace-Control system, and risk-mitigation tools such as PFMEA, PPAP, first-article inspection, and 8D problem solving. Its stated differentiation is the ability to act as a full-lifecycle electronics partner from ideation through volume production.

name: Whaling City Solar
old_description: Whaling City Solar is a residential and small-commercial solar installation company based in New Bedford, MA. We serve customers throughout the South Coast and Cape Cod. The company was founded in 2020 to create a better customer experience when purchasing solar equipment. We see many door-knocking, cold calling, and social media ad companies showing one picture of solar, while in reality, solar systems can take dozens of forms. We founded our company to tailor fit each and every array to its home and owners.
about:
Whaling City Solar was founded in 2020 in New Bedford, Massachusetts, to offer a better customer experience for residential and small-commercial solar purchases. The company was started by a team of engineers, project managers, and foremen who wanted to tailor each solar array to the specific home and owner, moving away from the high-pressure sales tactics common in the industry.

The firm handles the full installation process in-house, from initial site and financial assessment through permitting, installation, and commissioning. It manages all permitting paperwork—including Eversource interconnection agreements and town building and electrical permits—typically requiring two to five weeks for approvals. Installation crews usually complete a project in a single day, mounting rails and modules on the roof while simultaneously upgrading the electrical panel and inverters. The company works with equipment from brands such as REC, Solaria, and QCell modules; Enphase IQ8+ microinverters and SolarEdge string inverters; and Enphase Encharge, FranklinWH, and SPAN battery storage systems.

Whaling City Solar serves homeowners and small businesses across southeastern Massachusetts and Cape Cod, with recent projects completed in Mattapoisett, New Bedford, and Westport. Its service area covers the South Coast region, where the team lives and works, giving them familiarity with local weather, inspectors, and lenders.

The company differentiates itself by operating without sales commissions or call centers, providing direct access to technical staff. It promises a clear quote within 24 hours of a site visit, including costs, timelines, and projected financials, and emphasizes transparent, straightforward service rooted in the local community.

name: White Sands Woodworks Inc.
old_description: Karl is such an exceptional gentlemen. We are so thankful to have come across his business. Karl provides quality work and attention to detail. Being able to find someone who specializes in wood work was important, but finding someone who is extremely passionate about what he does was the icing on the cake. If you’re looking for someone to depend on to make your vision come true and you enjoy a positive environment, Karl is your guy.
about:
White Sands Woodworks operates from Alamogordo, New Mexico, near White Sands National Park and Holloman Air Force Base. The company was established in 2014 by Karl Peter, a German native who spent nearly three decades in the German Air Force before retiring to pursue a lifelong passion for woodworking and blacksmithing. The business is family operated and blends German craftsmanship traditions with American practicality, rooted in Karl’s early years restoring antique furniture alongside his father in Germany.

The shop produces custom wood and metal pieces, ranging from cutting boards and epoxy river tables to furniture, cabinetry, hand-forged knives, and military-themed displays such as challenge coin holders and flag cases. Work combines traditional joinery and blacksmithing with modern laser cutting and engraving, allowing for personalized details on materials that include domestic hardwoods, African exotic species, birch, acrylic, and stones like turquoise. Output is made to order in a small workshop; no facility size or headcount is disclosed.

Customers span active-duty and retired military personnel seeking commemorative gifts, homeowners ordering bespoke furniture and décor, and businesses needing custom pieces for office or retail settings. Reviews highlight projects such as an overnight plaque for a ceremony, restoration of a century-old oak table, and a precision acrylic component for a planetary model installed in Alamogordo.

The company emphasizes a fusion of old-world craftsmanship and current technology, positioning itself as a source for heirloom-quality items tailored to each client’s vision. Karl Peter’s background in antique restoration and his dedication to the craft are cited as the foundation for the business’s focus on quality, artistry, and personal service.

Today the shop delivers printed circuit board assembly (through-hole and surface-mount with fine-pitch capability down to 5 mm), wiring harness and cable assemblies, chassis wiring, conformal coating, and full electro-mechanical box builds. Juki placement machines handle automated SMT work, while manual and machine soldering lines support high-reliability requirements. The facility supports volumes ranging from small batches to large-scale production runs, backed by a staff whose collective experience exceeds 500 years.

Customers span Fortune 500 manufacturers such as IBM, Caterpillar, Teledyne Brown Engineering, and Boeing, as well as federal agencies including NASA and the Department of Defense. The company also serves small businesses with specialized needs, providing contract manufacturing across aerospace, defense, industrial equipment, and commercial electronics sectors.

Whitesburg emphasizes a zero-defect mission documented in a corporate quality manual that incorporates MIL‑STD‑45208 inspection requirements, ISO/IEC 17025‑accredited test and calibration, and IPC‑J‑STD‑001/IPC‑A‑610 soldering and acceptance standards. A CFC‑free, EPA‑compliant cleaning process and controlled handling of confidential data round out the quality framework.

old_description: Founded in 2020 during the global pandemic, WhyGen Solar was built to empower sales professionals in the solar industry. CEO Aaron Rice saw a critical gap—most companies focus on profits, not their sales force.
about:
WhyGen Solar was founded in 2020 in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, during the COVID-19 pandemic. CEO Aaron Rice started the company after recognizing a gap in the solar industry: most firms prioritized profits over their sales force. Rice, influenced by Simon Sinek's "Start With Why," built the business around the idea that supporting sales representatives leads to better customer outcomes.

The company provides residential and commercial solar installation services across New Mexico, Arizona, and Colorado. Its offerings include direct purchase, loan financing, and lease or power-purchase agreements, each backed by warranties covering parts, labor, and in some cases system production. WhyGen Solar does not manufacture equipment; it designs and installs systems using third-party components.

The customer base spans homeowners seeking to reduce utility bills and businesses aiming for sustainable energy. Residential clients can choose from zero-down options with tax incentives, while commercial customers receive tailored system designs. The company cites its BBB A+ rating in the Southwest Region as a marker of service quality.

WhyGen Solar differentiates itself by investing heavily in sales-rep training and support, arguing that empowered representatives deliver a superior client experience. This people-first philosophy, rooted in the founder's reading of "Start With Why," remains the core of its operational model.

David was in charge of the financial side of the business, while Allen served as the head of the shop. To this day, both of them still serve as John’s right-hand men. about:
Wil-Clair Sheet Metal was founded in 1999 in Kansas City, Missouri, by John Svetlecic after he left a previous sheet metal shop following a disagreement over company direction. He brought along two former employees, David Ogle to handle finances and Allen Kubicki to run the shop floor, both of whom remain with the company today.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, offering five-axis waterjet cutting (on an Omax Maxiem 1530), fiber laser cutting, certified welding, metal rolling, press brake forming, plasma cutting, and tile cutting. It also provides engineering and drawing services to develop economical designs. The facility has expanded over the years to accommodate increased capacity, though specific square footage and annual part volumes are not disclosed.

Wil-Clair serves a diverse industrial base including food processing (Kellogg’s, Tyson), commercial signage (Procter & Gamble), plumbing and mechanical contracting (Stine-Nichols Plumbing), construction and entertainment (Worlds of Fun), and general industrial fabrication (CDI, Impact Fabrication). Customers range from large national brands to local design-build firms.

The company emphasizes a problem-solving approach dubbed the “Blacksmith Sheet Metal methodology,” with CEO John Svetlecic stating, “We’ll do whatever it takes to get the job done for our clients.” Differentiators include direct access to leadership—calls are often answered by the CEO, shop superintendent, or foreman—a team of experienced craftsmen, and investment in modern equipment such as five-axis waterjet and fiber laser technology.

The company produces solid-wood furniture using 100 percent slow-grown hardwoods — red oak, maple, cherry, and quarter-sawn white oak — sourced from the Northern Appalachian Mountains and kiln-dried for consistent moisture content. Woodco now manufactures its own furniture lines and also stocks complementary American-made pieces, offering customization on dimensions, wood species, and finish.

Woodco serves residential customers directly through its Van Buren showroom and ships nationwide, while also maintaining a wholesale channel for trade buyers. Its early history as a parts supplier to furniture factories across the country gives it experience in both component and finished-goods production.

The business was built on controlling quality from lumber selection through final assembly, a response to the decline of domestic manufacturing. The Pierces emphasize sustainable forestry practices, domestic sourcing, and a made-to-order approach that they say yields heirloom-quality pieces backed by personal customer service.

The company states its differentiation lies in "sensing the power of light" – harnessing the full spectrum, visible and invisible, to add intelligence to illumination. 406 Processing & Taxidermy operates from Great Falls, Montana, where it runs a whole-animal butchery and taxidermy shop. The business is locally owned and operated by award-winning taxidermist Dylan Lencioni, an avid hunter and fisherman who frames the venture as a family endeavor. No founding year is disclosed in the available sources.

The company provides year-round processing for farmers, ranchers, and hunters. Its core services include wild-game processing (deer, elk, antelope), livestock slaughter and processing with an on-ranch harvesting option, European skull mounts cleaned using a beetle-based method that preserves bone integrity, and full taxidermy mounts produced by Brad Lencioni. The facility sits at 900 12th Street North; no square footage, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Customers are primarily central Montana ranchers who need USDA-style slaughter and cut-and-wrap services, as well as individual hunters during the fall season. The website lists set prices for European mounts — $195 for elk, $160 for deer — and notes that beetle cleaning is available for buffalo, bear, beef, and small game skulls.

The company emphasizes two differentiators: a guarantee that each client receives meat only from the animal they delivered, and the convenience of mobile on-ranch slaughtering. The beetle-cleaning process is highlighted as a way to maintain natural bone structure without shrinkage, and the taxidermy work is positioned as trophy-quality, using premium forms and materials.

Doug Cone had worked in the metal industry since 1983, progressing from stacker to plant manager and franchise owner, while Jill Cone joined him in 2008 after a nursing career; together they launched AZ Metals after completing a prior franchise agreement.

The company stocks and distributes a wide range of metals — including carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, brass, bronze, copper, and alloy and tool steels — in shapes such as sheet, plate, tube, pipe, bar, and structural profiles. It maintains over 19,000 line items and offers value‑added processing: shearing (Cincinnati 1810 and Pexto 12U52 squaring shears), band sawing (Hyd‑Mech S20 and Kama saws), punching and notching (GEKA Bendicrop 60S ironworker), bending (Chicago mechanical brake and Baileigh magnetic brake), drilling, and custom fabrication. All orders are cut to size with no minimum quantity.

AZ Metals serves residential, commercial, and industrial customers across the Phoenix East Valley and ships nationwide. Its client base includes builders, landscapers, repair and maintenance departments, fabrication shops, DIY enthusiasts, and local handymen.

The company’s stated mission is to meet the needs of both wholesale and retail buyers by providing an extensive selection of metals cut to size with exceptional service. It differentiates itself through no‑minimum‑order policies, same‑day local delivery, and the ability to source hard‑to‑find alloys.

old_description: Billions of tons of plastic have been made in the past decade, but experts estimate that 91% of that plastic hasn't been recycled. AZ Plastic, Inc. wants to put a dent in that statistic. We recycle used plastics into resin pellets, which our clients can use as an eco-friendly substitute for new plastics.
about:
AZ Plastics, Inc. was founded in 2018 in Chicago Heights, Illinois, a south suburb of Chicago. The company was started by a team with extensive experience processing HDPE and HMW plastics, aiming to recycle used plastics into resin pellets as an eco-friendly substitute for virgin plastics.

The company operates a state-of-the-art facility where it buys used plastics — ranging from detergent bottles to industrial drums — and power washes, shreds, and converts them into pellets. It processes HDPE (high-density polyethylene) containers, plastic skids, injection-grade products, HDPE Frac Melt (milk jugs, shampoo bottles), and HMW (high molecular weight) plastics such as IBCs, drums, and pipes. The facility includes an in-house lab for quality assurance.

AZ Plastics serves a global customer base across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. Its recycled resin pellets are used by manufacturers seeking sustainable alternatives for new plastic products. The company is a member of the Reusable Industrial Packaging Association (RIPA), indicating engagement with industrial packaging and recycling sectors.

The company was started to address the environmental impact of single-use plastics, with a goal to eliminate single-use plastics entirely and promote environmental responsibility among employees, vendors, and customers.

They began as buyers of special constructions, overstocks, and discontinued commodities, leveraging long-standing relationships with wire and cable manufacturers.

The company operates as a master distributor of industrial, commercial, and specialty wire and cable. It maintains a vast inventory valued at $65 million across nine regional distribution centers nationwide. Services include cutting to length with no cut or reel charges, paralleling and Wemco services, stripping, coiling, shrink-wrapping, special packaging, blind shipments, and same-day shipping or will-call pickup. Residential applications cover NM-B, SER, SEU, landscape lighting, and submersible pump cable. Utility customers need ACSR, AAC, quadraplex, triplex, MV-105, and bare copper for power transmission.

The founders aimed to simplify the business by focusing on inventory depth, service, and client value. The company emphasizes no minimum order charges, same-day shipping, and a diverse inventory to act as a one-source distributor for hard-to-find items.

old_description: Millions of patients with Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, brain cancer, epilepsy, and other neurological disorders depend on therapies that must reach precise locations within the brain to be effective. about:
Actuated Medical, Inc. is based in Bellefonte, Pennsylvania. The company operates as a clinical-stage medical device developer focused on technologies for precise brain access.

The company's core product is the NeuralGlider® Precision Brain Access Platform, which uses electronically controlled ultrasonic motion to maintain trajectory during insertion through brain tissue. Preclinical studies have demonstrated precise delivery of AAV gene therapy to deep brain targets using smaller-diameter cannulas, resulting in healthier tissue at the insertion site and reduced drug reflux.

Actuated Medical serves the neurology, neurosurgery, and gene therapy sectors, targeting conditions such as Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, brain cancer, and epilepsy. Its platform is designed for use by neurosurgeons and researchers delivering brain-directed therapies, including drug delivery, implants, and gene therapies.

The company was founded to address what it describes as a fundamental bottleneck in brain therapeutics: the challenge of accurate delivery to precise brain targets. The NeuralGlider platform aims to improve target accuracy, reduce tissue trauma, and enable smaller-diameter access, thereby supporting more effective delivery across multiple brain-directed therapy categories.

Cable, and Andre Lukovic engineering, procurement, and design.

The company designs and manufactures custom Cable Bus systems — insulated power cables housed in ventilated metal enclosures — for service entrances, main feeders, and distribution applications in power generation and industrial plants. Each system is engineered to job-specific requirements, with ampacity ratings from 800 to 6,000 amperes and voltage classes ranging from 480 volts to 69 kilovolts. Production includes custom-fabricated cable support blocks, short-circuit braces welded into enclosure sections, and covers with 50 percent ventilation to achieve free-air conductor ratings.

Advanced Cable Bus serves power generation facilities, industrial manufacturers, telecommunications data centers, and renewable energy projects. Named clients include Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. and Irving Consumer Products. The company sells through a nationwide network of manufacturer's representatives, with direct sales coverage in South Carolina and surrounding states.

The founders set out to deliver safe, reliable, maintenance-free power systems that are easy to install, backed by personalized service at every project stage. Their design uses uniform conductor spacing and short-circuit bracing rated to withstand 100 kA RMS symmetrical fault currents, reducing cable count compared to tray or conduit installations and lowering overall project cost.

name: All European Auto Supply
old_description: Here is a great explanation from Wikipedia when searching "OEM": "An Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is a company that produces parts and equipment that may be marketed by another manufacturer. For example, if Acme Manufacturing Co. makes power cords that are used on IBM computers, Acme is an OEM. The term is also used in several other ways, which causes ambiguity. It sometimes means the maker of a system that includes other companies' subsystems, an end-product producer, an automotive part that is manufactured by the same company that produced the original part used in the automobile's assembly, or a value-added reseller." "When referring to auto parts, OEM refers to the manufacturer of the original equipment, that is, the parts assembled and installed during the construction of a new vehicle. In contrast, aftermarket parts are those made by companies other than the OEM, which might be installed as replacements after the car comes out of the factory. For example, if Ford used Autolite spark plugs, Exide batteries, Bosch fuel injectors, and Ford's own engine blocks and heads when building a car, then car restorers and collectors consider those to be the OEM parts. Other-brand parts would be considered aftermarket, such as Champion spark plugs, DieHard batteries, Kinsler fuel injectors, and BMP engine blocks and heads. Many auto parts manufacturers sell parts through multiple channels, for example to car makers for installation during new-vehicle construction, to car makers for resale as automaker-branded replacement parts, and through general merchandising supply chains. Any given brand of part can be OE on some vehicle models and aftermarket on others".

old_description: As a global manufacturer of compostable sealant, barrier sealant films, and laminates, we serve a diverse range of industries including food, beverage, medical, personal care, office, industrial, and other consumer packaged goods (CPG) segments.
about:
Earthfirst Films operates as a division of Aluf Plastics from its headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, with additional manufacturing sites in Orangeburg, New York, and Sulphur Springs, Texas. The business traces its roots to 1949 when Joe Tatem founded Plastic Suppliers as a privately held corporation in Blackwood, New Jersey. Over decades the company expanded through distribution and converting centers across the United States and Europe, beginning film manufacturing in Columbus in 1976. In 2022 the organization rebranded its biopolymer portfolio globally as Earthfirst®, and in 2025 it was acquired by API.

The Columbus campus houses two primary facilities: a blown film plant and a cast-and-tenter extrusion plant Core processes include blown film extrusion, cast and tenter extrusion, lamination, slitting, and converting. An on-site laboratory equipped with two lab extruders performs tensile, barrier, optical, FTIR, and microscopy testing. The company holds several patents on compostable sealant films and offers small-batch production with fast prototyping of laminates for brand owners.

Products target food, beverage, medical, personal care, office, industrial, and broader consumer packaged goods segments. Customers range from brand owners seeking compostable sealant and barrier sealant films to converters needing flow-wrap, shrink-sleeve, and laminated structures. The portfolio includes PLA-based films, PHA-based home-compostable grades, and other biobased polymers.

The company states its mission is to create sustainable solutions through open collaboration. Its differentiation rests on over 20 years of biopolymer extrusion experience, patented blown-extrusion technology for thin-gauge films, SQF-certified food-grade production at the blown film facility, and a commitment to rapid prototyping that acts as an incubator for new packaging ideas.

ASI's service portfolio spans the full development cycle: design and integration, prototype fabrication, wafer-level test, system and reliability testing, and final assembly of packaged ICs and test chips. Customers include developers of flexible hybrid electronics, wearable sensors, and internet-of-things devices who require rapid prototyping and low-volume production of ultra-thin packages. about:
Amtech Systems, Inc. (ASYS) is headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Founded in 1981, the company operates as a global supplier of semiconductor equipment and materials through four wholly-owned subsidiaries: BTU International, Entrepix Inc., PR Hoffman, and Intersurface Dynamics.

The company designs, manufactures, and sells capital equipment and consumables for semiconductor fabrication, advanced packaging, and electronics assembly. Its process portfolio spans chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), lapping, polishing, cleaning, etching, belt and diffusion furnaces, and solder reflow ovens, including the TrueFlat line for ultra-thin substrates. Amtech maintains eight locations across five countries.

Customers include integrated circuit fabricators, OEMs, materials suppliers, defense contractors, and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) providers. The equipment serves end markets such as mobile, computing, industrial, automotive, telecommunications, medical, and power semiconductors, with high-volume reflow systems deployed for AI semiconductor device packaging.

Amtech states its differentiator is the quality of its products and customer service, positioning itself as a supplier of high-quality solutions. Its growth strategy focuses on the silicon carbide and power semiconductor sectors, leveraging subsidiaries like Entrepix for CMP services and BTU for thermal processing equipment.

Anco manufactures a range of stainless steel processing equipment, including process tanks, mixing tanks, milk silos, pasteurizers, homogenizers, cheese vats, butter churns, and COP wash tanks. The company collaborates with experienced engineers to provide start-to-finish solutions, and its customer roster includes major brands such as Coca-Cola, Starbucks, Unilever, Godiva Chocolate, and McDonald's.

The company serves the food, dairy, beverage, cosmetic, and chemical industries. Its equipment is used by large-scale producers as well as smaller processors needing sanitary stainless steel systems. Anco's product line covers accessories, all-in-one factory systems, and specialized units like dome-top and wing-top pasteurizers.

Trevor Anderson founded Anco to help customers grow their businesses through reliable, detail-oriented equipment. The company emphasizes a pragmatic approach, attention to detail, and collaboration with seasoned engineers to deliver solutions that meet strict sanitary standards.

old_description: and build custom furniture, collector pieces, and studio line furniture for homeowners, collectors, and designers who want something real—furniture with presence, intention, and longevity. Every piece that leaves my shop is made by hand, using traditional joinery and carefully selected hardwoods, right here in Washington State.
about:
Anderson Woodworks LLC operates from a shop in Yelm, Washington, where founder Brian Anderson builds custom furniture, cabinetry, and one-of-a-kind collector pieces. An Olympia-area native, Anderson spent roughly twelve years in custom home building before opening his own shop, applying that experience to pieces that must live in real houses. The business is structured as an LLC with Anderson as the sole craftsman; every piece passes through his hands alone.

The shop produces dining tables, desks, consoles, kitchen and bath cabinetry, library built-ins, and closet systems, all using hand-cut dovetail and mortise-and-tenon joinery rather than screws or staples. Anderson also offers a Studio Line of proven designs built to order and a Collector Line of singular works that may include marquetry inlay and experimental forms. In addition to fabrication, he provides furniture-led interior design consultations—space planning, material direction, and layout guidance—charging fees for design direction and full-room design packages. Projects begin with a free on-site estimate in Thurston and Pierce Counties, followed by a paid design phase before any wood is cut.

Clients include homeowners, collectors, and interior designers throughout the South Sound region—Olympia, Lacey, Tumwater, Tacoma, and Gig Harbor—with collector pieces shipped nationally. The service model skips catalogs and middlemen; Anderson designs, builds, and delivers each piece, while installation is coordinated with the client’s contractor.

Anderson positions the business on the premise that furniture should shape the room, not follow trends. He emphasizes traditional joinery that takes longer but yields pieces intended to last generations, and he frames his role as helping clients make clear, confident decisions so their homes feel grounded and intentional.

about:
Anglims Western Metalworks Inc operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico. The business was founded in 1981 by Clyde and Sandy Buckelew as a family-owned venture that began in a garage as a one-man shop. In 2010 the Buckelews retired and sold the company to Kevin and Jennifer Anglim, who had previously run a mobile welding and fabrication business.

The shop provides metal fabrication, welding, and precision cutting services. Core processes include fabrication in steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and sheet metal; MIG, TIG, and stick welding; 5-axis waterjet cutting on a Maxiem 1530 (OMAX) system; CNC cutting and shearing; machining; tube forming; and metal sign production. Work is performed in-house, with on-site fabrication and welding available for projects that cannot be transported. The waterjet offers a 10'0" x 5'2" cutting envelope and holds linear positional accuracy of ±0.0030" and repeatability of ±0.0010".

Customers span agriculture, clean-room technology, government and public utilities, healthcare, manufacturing, mining, restaurants, and facility support. Corporate and institutional clients have included PNM, the General Electric Airplane Engine Plant, Motorola, Intel, Rio Grande Concrete Plant, Sandia National Laboratories, and New Mexico Air Force bases, as well as local farmers and dairymen.

The company emphasizes attention to detail, precise craftsmanship, fairness, and customer service. It states that quality welds should be stronger than the base metal and visually seamless, a standard met through experienced welders and investment in equipment.

AnTek Inc. was established in 2005 in North Arlington, New Jersey, minutes from New York City. The company operates under the AnTek Products Corp. name and focuses on power solutions for a broad customer base.

The company designs and manufactures toroidal transformers for audio and CNC applications, with a product range spanning 10 VA to 4 kVA. It also produces tube amplifier power transformers, single-ended and push-pull output transformers, steel powder-coated amplifier chassis, and a line of unregulated power supplies rated from 50 W to over 1,000 W. AnTek serves customers from hobbyist DIY builders to professional audio and electronics manufacturers. name: Applied Molding Technologies, LLC
old_description: Founded in 2006, Applied Molding Technologies delivers thermoplastic injection and thermoset compression, transfer and injection molding from Frederic, Wisconsin, serving customers globally, with new tooling built domestically and off-shore.
about:
Applied Molding Technologies, LLC was founded in 2006 in Frederic, Wisconsin. The company began at a time when conventional wisdom held that domestic manufacturing could not compete with low-wage overseas producers, and its founders built the business on the premise that a fundamentally different operating model was required to succeed.

The shop provides thermoplastic injection molding on all-electric presses ranging from 55 to 850 tons of clamp force, and thermoset compression, transfer, and injection molding on presses from 150 to 300 tons. It also offers value-added mechanical assembly including heat-staking, ultrasonic insertion, sub-assemblies, kitting, and packaging. Production runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year on a four-shift rotation designed to minimize start-up and shut-down scrap. The facility handles low- to high-volume runs and high-cavitation tooling, with new molds built domestically or off-shore and maintained in-house.

Applied Molding serves a global customer base with parts that require heat resistance, dielectric strength, and long-term stability, such as electrical and dielectric components and large or thick-section parts. As a pure custom molder with no proprietary product lines, the company scales its engineering, quality, and program-management support to each customer’s requirements, from full-scope program support to straightforward production orders.

The company was designed from first principles around three core attributes: efficiency, customization, and adaptability. Its continuous 24/7 schedule, lean headcount, and in-house core capabilities are intended to reduce fixed overhead and improve repeatability. Management emphasizes continuous improvement and structured retrospection to rebuild processes when conditions change.

about:
Aries Electronics Inc was founded in 1972 in Bristol, Pennsylvania. The company began as a supplier of electrical sockets and interconnect products, growing into a manufacturer of specialized components for integrated circuit devices.

The company produces a range of interconnect solutions including production IC sockets, test and burn-in sockets, high-frequency RF sockets, PCB and IC adapters, cable assemblies, and its patented Correct-A-Chip® limited-depth pin assemblies. Aries also offers custom engineering services and molds engineered plastics such as UL 94V-0 rated PEEK and Ultem to tolerances under 0.2 mm pitch.

Aries serves original equipment manufacturers and electronic assembly companies across semiconductor, telecommunications, aerospace, and industrial electronics sectors. Its components are used in IC devices, electronic machinery, and custom OEM applications worldwide.

The business differentiates itself through custom design and production capabilities, allowing special materials, platings, sizes, and configurations based on quantity requirements. The Correct-A-Chip technology eliminates the need for new PCB layouts when substituting integrated circuits, providing a cost-effective solution for obsolescence and design changes.
